A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same partitioned-supervision framework. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite the revised title and reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, an IVW weighting ablation, and ADAS/AFlow agent-search experiments in Tables 1-2 and Figures 2-4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds derived reference-deviation results and qualitative analysis of learned agent workflows in Appendices L-M.

M1.justification: The complementary-label correction, IVW and ML estimators, labeling protocol, and their use in ADAS/AFlow remain unchanged. Appendix M newly describes learned workflows without reporting a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Coverage remains MMLU-Pro, MedQA-USMLE, GPQA, MATH-MC, EDINET and its extended version, and Medical Abstracts. The new case study examines agents from the existing Medical Abstracts setting; the proposed debugging application is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain the same estimator comparisons. Figure 3 retains CoT, CoT-SC, Self-Refine, LLM Debate, Step-back Abstraction, Quality-Diversity and Role Assignment alongside ADAS and AFlow. New Table 3 reuses the existing estimator set.

E3.justification: Appendix L adds explicitly reported evaluation metrics: absolute percentage-point deviation from Ord-Eval and its average across benchmarks. These are derived from existing results; benchmark construction, sample sizes, model choices, validation/test splits and search procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix M adds a qualitative case study of ADAS principle extraction followed by classification and AFlow review, candidate generation and ensembling. The existing IVW sample-count ablation and raw-versus-transformed feedback analysis remain unchanged in Figures 2 and 4.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds, across-seed standard deviations and average within-run standard deviations in Tables 1-2. Standard-error and confidence-interval procedures, and the three AFlow validation runs, are retained. No new uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1-2 retain all numerical entries, and Figures 2-4 retain identical plotted results. New Table 3 derives reference errors from Table 1, including average deviations of 1.42 for IVW, 1.48 for ML and 1.92 for Ord. Appendix M adds qualitative workflow findings, not evidence of improved benchmark performance.

T1.justification: The estimator equations, variance analysis, deviation bounds and Newton/IVW derivation retain their mathematical substance. The Corollary 1 and Theorem 2 proofs move from the main text to Appendices A and E. Notation changes and relocated fixed-weight qualifications do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same main contributions: complementary-label accuracy estimation, variance characterization, mixed estimators and weak-feedback agent design. Adding 'Towards' to the title and revising the self-improvement wording do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5 expands applicability discussion to expert noise and overlapping expertise, open-ended tasks, unavailable complementary labels and ambiguous ground truth, and suggests debugging as a possible application. Appendix M additionally interprets weak feedback as shaping structured, interpretable workflows.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility statement acknowledging API model changes, updates the repository link, and documents selected agents' internal stages, including three AFlow candidates in Figure 5. Previously reported splits, prompts and implementation adaptations are retained in Appendix J.

R1.justification: v2 adds Feng et al. (2020) and Ishiguro et al. (2022) for multiple and noisy complementary labels, plus safety references in the ethics statement. The central positioning relative to scalable oversight, weak supervision and agent discovery remains unchanged. Publication updates and the deduplicated Reflexion reference are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording, title/header and notation edits, moves two proofs and benchmark details into appendices, and adds discussion and disclosure sections. Most existing exposition and the overall methodological and experimental narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised, Figures 2-3 are reduced and repositioned, and Table 1 gains an estimator legend. Table 3 and the two-panel workflow Figure 5 are added. Existing quantitative charts preserve their data, with limited changes to the overall document layout.

improvement.justification: The new limitations and reproducibility discussions clarify practical boundaries, while Table 3 and Figure 5 make existing findings easier to assess. These are limited transparency gains rather than stronger experimental validation. Smaller plots reduce readability, and Appendix M's claims about feedback producing interpretable behavior exceed its illustrative evidence, tempering the improvement.
